128570.overview: Sub Chase is a portable electronic game released by Mattel Electronics brand in 1978.

128741.overview: Snoopy Tennis is a Game & Watch video game released in 1982 by Nintendo. The game was very successful, perhaps due to the Snoopy label, with Nintendo producing an estimated 1,200,000 worldwide. In the game, you control Snoopy, moving him up and down to make him hit the oncoming tennis balls with your racket. It was released on the Wide Screen format. A version of the game was released as a keychain title under the miniclassics label. The control button leaflet, which was only present in this game's box and Fire Attack's, showcases various characters from the Peanuts franchise. Unsurprisingly, due to licensing issues, the game was not released in any of the Game & Watch video games, though it was mentioned in Super Smash Bros. Brawl for the Wii.

132347.overview: The Table Top version of Snoopy has a bigger screen, enhanced color graphics and sound effects due to the color LCD (CLCD) model and larger housing. The player controls Snoopy, who has to prevent the musical notes from Schroeder's piano reaching the top level of the screen, where Woodstock is sleeping. The player controls Snoopy with his hammer, who has to jump from platform to platform to hit the floating music notes. In Game A one only has to deal with three music notes, whilst the pacing and the amount of music notes (four instead of three) to handle are increasing in Game B. After every 100 points Lucy, sleeping at the bottom will kick Schroeder's small piano.

132348.overview:
Snoopy is a Game & Watch game released as a part of the Table Top series on June 5, 1983, and as a part of the Panorama series on August 30, 1983. It was the first game in the Panorama series. It is a single-screen single-player Game & Watch. Hirokazu Tanaka composed the game music.

Schroeder plays the piano. The player moves Snoopy between platforms and uses a mallet to hit rising notes before they reach Woodstock.

134994.overview:
Soldier Fighter (Model CG-86) is a rare, vintage handheld electronic game released by Casio in 1984. Part of Casio's popular 1980s "brick" style pocket game lineup, it is a highly sought-after piece of retro gaming history.

The game features old-school digital graphics and retro electronic sound effects where players control a soldier fighting off incoming enemies. Because these individual handheld systems were largely replaced by multi-game consoles, working original units have become prime collector's items.

147984.overview: Safari is a portable electronic game released by VTech under the Time & Fun brand in 1981. Apparently, this device was created in the likeness of the then popular series of portable electronic games Game & Watch from Nintendo.

153041.overview: Another game from the Time & Fun series. This is the French release by Ludotronic.

154257.overview:
Grandstand Scramble is a highly popular vintage 1982 electronic tabletop mini-arcade game released in the UK by Grandstand (originally manufactured by Epoch in Japan). Officially licensed from Konami, it was based on the iconic 1981 side-scrolling arcade hit Scramble, bringing the "pew-pew" space-shooter experience right into 1980s living rooms.

Unlike the scrolling maps of the arcade version, hardware limits mean the tabletop variant focuses on static screens with waves of oncoming targets. Players start with 3 lives and must fight through 5 distinct game phases to destroy the enemy headquarters.

159971.overview:
Super Mario Bros. is a Game & Watch game released as a part of the Crystal Screen series on June 25, 1986, and as a part of the New Wide Screen series on March 8, 1988. It was the first game in the Crystal Screen series. It is a single-screen single-player Game & Watch.

It was also made available as a prize for winners of the Famicon's F-1 Grand Prix tournament on August 1, 1987 with code YM-901-S. It is a single-screen single-player Game & Watch with a yellow case. It came in a plastic box modeled after Disk-kun, the character Nintendo used to advertise the Famicom Disk System. This edition is the rarest of all Game & Watch models, as only 10,000 units of this version were produced and it was never available for retail sale.

Mario has to go through levels to save Princess Toadstool (also known as Peach) similar to the NES game.

Super Mario Bros. was rereleased as part of the Nintendo Mini Classics 1998 in Game & Watch Gallery 3 for Game Boy Color in 1999.

162014.overview: As Sparky, players have to shoot blocks by keeping a ball afloat with puffs of air, creating a game similar to Breakout or Arkanoid. The player earns a point for erasing a green block, two points for a blue block, and three points for a red block. When the player clears a display, they will earn five points for every unit remaining on the bonus meter. The next display will contain more blocks, with the maximum being 18. If the player erases all but the red blocks and then hits all the red blocks once to make them flash, the player will be awarded 30 points. Eventually, blocks that require two hits to break will appear, as well as unbreakable barriers that get in the player's way. If a ball falls to the bottom, the player receives a miss. At 300 points, any misses the player has will be removed. The player receives a Game Over when they have three misses.

162015.overview: A bandit named the Wily Bomber is dropping bombs from the roof of a bank onto a safe, and the player as the bank guard must catch them in a pipe. The player receives a point for every bomb they catch. The pipe can hold only three bombs, however, so the player must dispose of them in the right or left corner as they pile up. As the player disposes of bombs in the left corner, flaming torches will appear from the blast, which will eventually stop by themselves. If the player throws enough bombs into the left corner, the flaming torches will set fire to the Wily Bomber's arsenal, blowing it up and blasting him away, awarding the player 20 points. If a bomb hits the safe, the safe will blow open, and then the Wily Bomber will climb down and steal the money, penalizing the player with a miss. At 200 points, any misses the player has will be canceled. When the player gets three misses, they receive a Game Over.

164118.overview:
Squish is a Game & Watch game released as a part of the Multi Screen series on April 17, 1986. It is a dual-screen single-player Game & Watch. It opens like a compact, with an upper and lower screen.

It is similar to Devil World.

169644.overview:
Space Rescue depicts an interstellar emergency in which stranded astronauts float through debris fields while alien ships attack from above. The player commands a spacecraft charged with retrieving the lost crew before the aliens can capture or destroy them.


The player moves the rescue craft horizontally across the lower edge of the screen, timing movements to catch falling astronauts while avoiding incoming alien fire. Each astronaut successfully retrieved is counted toward the score, while missed rescues or collisions with enemy beams cost a life.

The game supports two modes: Game A (standard difficulty) and Game B (faster action and denser attack patterns). A visual “MISS” counter tracks errors, and the game ends after three misses or when all lives are lost.

169659.overview:
Shuttle Voyage places the player in control of a space shuttle navigating a hazardous flight path through outer space. The shuttle must cross successive traffic lanes of fast-moving spacecraft and debris to reach the opposite side of the screen safely, completing voyages through deep-space routes.

The display is divided into horizontal lanes filled with moving obstacles—rockets, satellites, and meteoroids—moving in alternating directions. The player moves the shuttle upward or downward between lanes using the two red arrow buttons on the left side of the unit, timing each movement to pass safely between hazards. Reaching the far side of the screen scores a point and returns the shuttle to the starting zone for another crossing. A collision with any object costs a life.

The calculator-style keypad beneath the display doubles as a clock and alarm interface when the unit is idle; the game uses only directional and “Forward” controls during play. Sound cues accompany movement, collisions, and successful crossings, using simple beeps typical of Tronica’s MG-series.

190421.overview: The Shadow is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on the movie The Shadow from 1994.

190422.overview: Skeleton Warriors is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on the animated TV series from 1994.

190423.overview: Sonic The Hedgehog is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on Sega's Sonic The Hedgehog video game.

190424.overview: Sonic The Hedgehog 2 is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on Sega's Sonic The Hedgehog 2 video game.

190425.overview: Space Harrier II is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on Sega's Space Harrier II arcade game.

190426.overview: Space Jam is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on the movie Space Jam from 1996.

190427.overview: Spider-Man is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics.

190495.overview:
Simon is an electronic game of memory skill invented by Ralph H. Baer and Howard J. Morrison, working for toy design firm Marvin Glass and Associates, with software programming by Lenny Cope. The device creates a series of tones and lights and requires a user to repeat the sequence. If the user succeeds, the series becomes progressively longer and more complex. Once the user fails or the time limit runs out, the game is over. The original version was manufactured and distributed by Milton Bradley and later by Hasbro after it took over Milton Bradley.  

Simon was launched in 1978 at Studio 54 in New York City and was an immediate success, becoming a pop culture symbol of the 1970s and 1980s.

190496.overview: This is from the original 1978 Star Wars merchandise line-up. Very difficult to play but pretty sound effects.

194732.overview:
The Pac-Man Coleco Tabletop is a tabletop arcade machine released by Coleco in 1981. It is based on handheld LCD game technology, and was intended for home use. It was released in Japan as Super Puck Monster.

The system features three modes - Pac-Man, Head-to-Head Pac-Man, and Eat & Run:

Pac-Man
A port of the original Pac-Man. A rather close port for the time period, especially for LCD technology. Some key features are missing however, most notably Fruit.

Head-to-Head Pac-Man
A two player co-op mode, with two Pac-Men on screen at once. Otherwise the same as the first mode.

Eat & Run
Guide Pac-Man to collect the four Power Pellets and bring them to the Ghost Box.

200086.overview: Mattel Electronics: Soccer is a classic handheld electronic game originally released in 1978 (Model 2678). Following the massive commercial success of Mattel's iconic 1977 Football game, Soccer capitalized on the late-1970s electronic gaming boom and helped cement Mattel Electronics as an industry powerhouse.

202750.overview:
Space Mission places the player in command of a lone rescue craft patrolling deep space. Astronauts drift helplessly after a disaster, while alien ships sweep in to attack. The mission: save as many stranded crew members as possible before the enemy fire overwhelms the rescue effort.

The player moves the spacecraft left and right to intercept falling astronauts and avoid the UFO’s energy blasts. Collecting an astronaut adds points; missing too many or taking a direct hit ends a life. The game offers two difficulty modes—Game A for standard play and Game B for faster, more aggressive enemy fire. Each life is represented by an icon of a shuttle crew at the top left. As in many early Tiger games, rhythm and reaction timing are the keys to survival.

204360.overview: Gakken's version of Stern/Konami's Super Cobra arcade game

210829.overview: Missile attack, later rebranded as Battlestar Galactica: Space Alert is a dedicated handheld action game in which the player must fight incoming missiles (Cylon Raiders in the re-release). To win the player must intercept 20 of them. The player can move to three positions and fire counter missiles (laser torpedoes in the re-release). In practice it comes down that red dots will come down the playfield and the player must move his or her red dot in its path and press the fire button which launches another red dot upwards. If it hits the enemy is intercepted.

210830.overview: The Star Fox Game Watch is a game in the appearance of a wristwatch that was developed by Nintendo and Nelsonic. It's a LCD game that could be achieved by buying two boxes of Kellogg's Corn Flakes and then sending the form back to Kellogg's for a free copy. The purpose of the game is to defeat the Attack Carrier while dodging several obstacles and while being airborne. There is a total of four levels in the game. When buying the game, a pair of earphones which are made for the game is included

422795.overview: This is a 2 player dexterity game where players are attempting to battle their way to the death star and destroy it. Players have to test their reaction speeds in tie fighter battles. The first one in each round to hit the correct weapon button, has one of 6 LEDs illuminated on the path to the Death Star in the middle. Once there, they have the chance to destroy the Death Star if they can win a final battle.

458869.overview: Super Mario Bros. 3 is a Mario game released within the Nelsonic Game Watch line of wristwatches. It was released in 1990, and is directly based on the Nintendo Entertainment System game of the same name. The game is alternatively titled Super Mario 3, as shown on the bezel, or Super Mario III in the included instruction booklet.

458871.overview: Super Mario World is a Mario game within the Nelsonic Game Watch line of wristwatches. It was released in 1991 as a tie-in product to the Super Nintendo Entertainment System game of the same name. Super Mario World came bundled with a pair of headphones.

476125.overview: The Tiger Electronics Sonic the Hedgehog 3 handheld video game is a classic LCD-style electronic game originally released in 1994, with a retro re-release by Hasbro in 2020. It features 6 stages of play, where players control Sonic and Tails to battle Dr. Eggman, collect Rings and Chaos Emeralds, and enter bonus stages.

476705.overview:
Space...the final frontier. These are the voyages of the Starship Enterprise. Its continuing mission: to explore strange new worlds, to seek out new life and new civilizations, to boldly go where no one has gone before™. But the Romulan empire has once again prompted a rash of galactic disturbances! Assume the command of the U.S.S. Enterprise as you steer clear of the dangers in space such as meteors and asteroids, while under attack from the Romulans! The fate of the U.S.S. Enterprise is in your hands!

Watch out, a Romulan warbird is in sight and is about to attack the "Starship Enterprise"!

Your "Phaser" is your only weapon of defense on the planet Romulus!*

476798.overview:
A vicious terrorist network, the Ring of Five, has kidnapped the children of the world's leaders. Your mission: to control Shinobi™ through 4 difficult and challenging stages to free the hostages and defeat their captors.

To aid you in your quest you have 3 weapons to use at various levels: A Shuriken, bomb and pistol. But beware! There are seven evil and craft kinds of terrorists including: Thugs, Gunmen, Mongos, Ninjas and Frogmen. So you must be at your best to defeat the leader at the end of every mission to come one step closer to a final victory.**

Stage #1 - Kill as many terrorists as you can with your Shuriken. You will gain a bonus energy bar and 100 points for each hostage you save.

Stage #2 - Each stage gets progressively harder with more and smarter enemies...now including the Gunmen and Mongo.

Stages #3 and 4 - Besides the Shuriken, your weapons now include Bombs and Pistols. But Watch Out! Frogmen randomly appear from the water so you must stay alert.

At the end of each mission Shinobi™ must face...and defeat the leader of that stage before moving on to the next level and ultimately winning the game.

477395.overview:
Step onto the court and get ready to play the game of your life - you're about to enter the world of Shaquille O'Neal - get ready for a Shaq Attaq! Think you know slam dunks? Try the Tomahawk Slam, the Slam Jam and the Monster Jam and watch Shaq shatter the backboard! Think you know rebounds? Watch Shaq "Put Back" the ball with the greatest of ease! Think you know double teaming? Two players are the least you'll need to guard Shaq! Think you're about to play the most exciting basketball game around? Go ask Shaq - if you dare!

Guide Shaq with your directional buttons to slam dunk, put back and score against a double team in three different games!

When your teammate shoots, control Shaq to rebound the ball and put it back on the rim! Score as many rebounds as you can within the time limit!

It's Shaq against a double team! Use your directional buttons to pull some smooth "Shaq Attaq" moves on the computer opponents!

Shaq goes for the Monster Jam! If your timing is perfect, you'll shatter the backboard and the screen will light up with a "MONSTER JAM" and a "THUNDERDUNK"!

477454.overview:
4 stages of spinball fun! Attack the Veg-O-Fortress! Fight through the Pinball Defense System!
Defeat Dr. Robotnik and free your pals! High score retained!

479141.overview:
The Springfield Nuclear Power Plant is having it's annual company picnic. The employee who's family wins a series of contests will become employee of the year. Homer wants to win so the Simpsons are each going to enter a different race and take home the award. Homer will enter a pie eating contest, Marge will enter a potato sack race, Bart will enter a frog jumping contest, Lisa will compete in a bicycle race, and little Maggie will enter a baby crawling race. All the Simpsons, all the fun!

Help Homer chow down on the donuts.

Play as Marge and hop to victory.

Show everyone Bart's frog is the fastest.

479360.overview:
Watch out! Bart and Lisa are in an adventure with radioactive dinosaurs!
Really cool sound effects! Bart and Lisa actually talk!
Watch out for Homersaurus! He's half man, half mutant dinosaur!

482404.overview: A Tronica handheld LCD game set around a spacecraft's passage through space hazards. Move between the available fixed positions and time each action to keep the run going. Successful responses add to the score, while repeated mistakes cut the attempt short. Its arcade challenge comes from reading the changing sequence on a compact display.

482405.overview: A goalkeeper defends against approaching shots in Tronica's handheld football game. Move to the position matching each incoming ball and make the save before it passes. The fixed LCD figures keep the controls simple while faster arrivals make later play more demanding. The goal is to build a high score without allowing too many failures.
